Check Sampling Precision of Fitted Bayesian Scales

Source: R/bayes_scale_diagnostics.R
diagnose_bayes_scales.Rd

Check chain mixing and simulation precision for the quantities you report from a sampled fit, the log scale of each landscape predictor and the between-group SDs. These derived quantities can mix differently from the individual parameters checked by the sampler's own diagnostics.

Usage

diagnose_bayes_scales(object, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975))

Arguments

object

A fitted multiScale_bayes() object. New diagnostics need the original unpermuted post-warmup chains from NUTS (sampler) or slice sampling (chains). Prepared, approximate, and compact fits return an unavailable report.

probs

Numeric vector of distinct probabilities strictly between 0 and 1. The default c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975) gives the median and the limits of a central 95% interval. Changing it changes which quantiles have their simulation error reported, not any diagnostic threshold.

Value

A list with these elements.

  • available, reason: whether full chain diagnostics could be computed, and an explanation when they could not.

  • raw_diagnostics: the sampler or approximation diagnostics stored in the fit, unchanged.

  • parameters: a data frame with one row per derived quantity. variable is an internal label. quantity is "log_distance", "scale_group_sd", or "response_group_sd". covariate, group, and a representative observation row identify it, and units states its units. rhat, ess_bulk, and ess_tail give the rank-normalized Rhat and the bulk and tail effective sample sizes.

  • quantiles: a data frame with the same identifying columns plus probability, the quantile estimate, and its Monte Carlo standard error mcse, both in the stated units. Undefined values are NA.

  • chains, iterations: the number of retained chains and of post-warmup iterations per chain, or NA when unavailable.

  • derived_passed: TRUE when there are at least two chains and every derived quantity has Rhat at most 1.01 and bulk and tail ESS of at least 100 per chain. NA when unavailable.

  • passed: TRUE when both the original sampler checks and the derived checks pass. NA when unavailable. For a slice fit sampled without the posterior package, the original parameter checks are computed here from the stored chains, while the fit's stored diagnostics stay as recorded.

  • criteria, notes: the fixed derived checks and their limits.

Read the report

ColumnAcceptableIf it fails
rhat1.01 or lessRefit with another seed and compare. A weak landscape effect leaves its scale poorly identified, and longer chains do not cure that
ess_bulk, ess_tailAt least 100 per chain (400 for four chains)Increase iter, or switch from slice sampling to NUTS
mcseNo fixed cutoff. Small next to the precision your question needsIncrease iter, and compare independent runs when an interval limit matters

Landscape scales are diagnosed on the natural log axis in map units, which avoids overflow and the infinite arithmetic distance moments that the hierarchical priors allow (see posterior_scales()). Exponentiate a log-distance quantile to express it in map units. Its MCSE is on the log axis, so an MCSE of 0.01 is about 1% of the distance. The MCSE is computational uncertainty, not a posterior interval or a biological SD. Scale-group SDs measure population variation in log distance. Response-group SDs use the response linear-predictor axis.

The posterior package computes rank-normalized Rhat, effective sample sizes, and quantile MCSE. A passed screen guarantees neither a precise tail endpoint nor discovery of every mode. Compare the MCSE with the precision your scientific decision needs, inspect independent runs when tails matter, and assess the likelihood and priors separately.

Why compact fits cannot be checked

Permuted or thinned stored draws cannot rebuild the original chain order or full-chain precision. Compact examples therefore keep their original diagnostic evidence but cannot provide new chain diagnostics. Laplace draws and weighted importance candidates are not MCMC chains, so use the stored numerical checks for those fits.

Draw chain plots

For chain plots in bayesplot, pass fit$chains for a slice fit, or rstan::extract(fit$sampler, permuted = FALSE, inc_warmup = FALSE) for a NUTS fit. vignette("v13-bayesian-scales", package = "multiScaleR") shows trace plots alongside these diagnostics, and vignette("v15-bayesian-computation", package = "multiScaleR") works through a fit that fails them.

See also

multiScale_bayes(), posterior_scales(), plot.multiScaleR_bayes(), diagnose_bayes_probabilities(), multiScaleR_bayes

Examples

# A stored slice fit that keeps its four original chains
shared <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "cache-bayesian-scales.rds",
  package = "multiScaleR"))$fit
if (requireNamespace("posterior", quietly = TRUE)) {
  report <- diagnose_bayes_scales(shared)
  print(report$passed)   # sampler and derived checks together
  # Agreement among chains and effective sample size for each log sigma
  print(report$parameters[c("covariate", "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail")])
  # Interval limits of log sigma, with their Monte Carlo standard errors
  q <- report$quantiles
  print(data.frame(q[c("covariate", "probability")],
                   sigma_m = exp(q$estimate), mcse_log = q$mcse))
}
#> [1] TRUE
#>   covariate     rhat  ess_bulk ess_tail
#> 1     land1 1.002665  905.3584  937.121
#> 2     land2 1.003975 1033.0974 1611.410
#>   covariate probability  sigma_m    mcse_log
#> 1     land1       0.025 180.7061 0.012290191
#> 2     land1       0.500 246.6455 0.005139396
#> 3     land1       0.975 344.4668 0.027488507
#> 4     land2       0.025 412.5682 0.006516360
#> 5     land2       0.500 501.1973 0.003116837
#> 6     land2       0.975 599.8042 0.005060544

# A compact fit keeps thinned, permuted draws and cannot be checked
example <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "bayesian-annual-example.rds",
                              package = "multiScaleR"))
compact <- diagnose_bayes_scales(example$fits$pooled)
compact$available  # FALSE: the compact example contains no full sampler
#> [1] FALSE
compact$reason
#> [1] "Full unpermuted MCMC chains are not retained. Stored permuted or thinned draws cannot recover original chain diagnostics."
